bib.title: WINOGRANDE: An Adversarial Winograd Schema Challenge at Scale

question: Have neural language models truly acquired commonsense on Winograd-style pronoun resolution, or do they exploit dataset biases that inflate their scores?
hypothesis: Existing WSC-style datasets contain spurious biases that models exploit; a larger, algorithmically debiased dataset will be much harder for models while staying easy for humans.
contributions: WINOGRANDE: 44k WSC-style problems built by crowdsourcing with WikiHow anchor-word constraints
AFLITE, a lightweight adversarial filtering algorithm using ensembles of linear classifiers over pre-computed RoBERTa embeddings
Baselines showing a 15-35% gap to human performance
State-of-the-art transfer results on WSC, DPR, COPA, KnowRef and Winogender, with a caution about overestimated commonsense

method.summary: Crowdworkers on AMT wrote twin sentences, three other workers validated them, and AFLITE removed instances whose RoBERTa embeddings let linear classifiers predict the label, leaving 12,282 debiased items. RoBERTa, BERT and other baselines were fine-tuned or run zero-shot on it, then RoBERTa fine-tuned on WinoGrande was transferred to related benchmarks.
method.task: Winograd-style pronoun resolution as binary fill-in-the-blank; benchmark construction and debiasing

datasets.name: WinoGrande (collected)
datasets.size: 77k questions (38k twins) collected; 53k valid after validation
datasets.source: Amazon Mechanical Turk; anchor word from random WikiHow article
datasets.preprocessing: Twins 15-30 words, at least 70% word overlap; validity by 3 workers: majority correct, unambiguous, not solvable by local word association

datasets.name: WinoGrande_debiased
datasets.source: AFLITE-filtered from 47k instances (6k used to fine-tune RoBERTa_embed discarded)
datasets.preprocessing: AFLITE with m=10,000, n=64, k=500, tau=0.75; about 1/3 of items are no longer twins

datasets.name: WinoGrande_all
datasets.source: debiased set plus 31k items filtered out by AFLITE
datasets.preprocessing: training set consists of twins; sizes XS 160, S 640, M 2,558, L 10,234, XL 40,938 used for the learning curve

datasets.name: WSC, PDP, SuperGLUE-WSC, DPR, KnowRef, COPA, Winogender
datasets.split: DPR train 1,200 / dev 122 (own split of 1,332); COPA dev 500 split into train 400 / dev 100; KnowRef public test 1.2k
datasets.preprocessing: WinoGrande converted to True/False binary form for SuperGLUE-WSC

other.input format: [CLS] context [SEP] option [SEP], option used as delimiter; [CLS] embedding classifies

models.name: RoBERTa_embed
models.architecture: RoBERTa fine-tuned on 6k instances (5k train, 1k val) to produce embeddings for AFLITE

models.name: WKH; Ensemble LMs (Trinh and Le 2018); GPT2

training.objective: binary classification of which answer option fills the blank (BERT/RoBERTa fine-tuning)
training.seeds: three random seeds in grid search; learning curve best of ten random seeds

other.transfer: same grid search for RoBERTa fine-tuned on WinoGrande train+dev then on targets

inference.samples: learning curve: best performance per training size over ten random seeds

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction of questions with correct option

metrics.name: KL divergence
metrics.definition: between distributions of PCA d1 for answer y=1 and y=2, bin size 100

metrics.name: Winogender |dF|,|dM|
metrics.definition: accuracy gap non-gotcha minus gotcha per gender

baselines: random data reduction and PMI filtering (for AFLITE)
eval.protocol: Dev/test accuracy; humans = majority vote of three crowd workers. Single reported numbers, no significance test stated.

limits: Authors concede transfer gains may partly reflect biases in the target benchmarks, not real commonsense progress.
Only RoBERTa/BERT-era models, no hyperparameters beyond grid ranges, optimizer, hardware or model size stated.
Learning-curve extrapolation (118K) is a log-linear fit.
Debiased training set alone yields chance performance; strong results need the 40,938-item WinoGrande_all train.
Human eval is crowd majority vote; later models (2020+) have saturated this benchmark.

terms.definition: lightweight adversarial filtering: ensembles of linear classifiers on precomputed embeddings remove instances whose label is predictable
pair of nearly identical questions with a trigger word that flips the correct answer
